questions.stem: A box plot has: minimum = 12, Q1 = 20, median = 28, Q3 = 35, maximum = 48. What is the interquartile range?
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 35 - 20 = 15. Option (a) calculates the range (48 - 12 = 36). The IQR represents the spread of the middle 50% of data.

questions.stem: Two box plots compare test scores. Box A: median = 60, IQR = 20. Box B: median = 55, IQR = 8. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Group A performed better on average and was more consistent
Group A performed better on average but was less consistent
Group B performed better on average and was more consistent
Group B performed better on average but was less consistent

questions.explanation: Group A has a higher median (60 > 55) so performed better on average. However, Group A has a larger IQR (20 > 8) so was less consistent. Group B's results were more tightly clustered around the median.

questions.stem: A box plot shows: minimum = 2, Q1 = 15, median = 25, Q3 = 30, maximum = 35. What does the shape of the box plot suggest about the data?

options.text: The lower half of data is more spread out than the upper half
Most data values are above the median
The data has no outliers so must be normally distributed

questions.explanation: Left whisker = Q1 - min = 15 - 2 = 13. Right whisker = max - Q3 = 35 - 30 = 5. Left box section = median - Q1 = 10. Right box section = Q3 - median = 5. Both the left whisker and left box section are larger, showing the lower half is more spread out (positive skew).

questions.stem: From a box plot: minimum = 8, Q1 = 18, median = 30, Q3 = 40, maximum = 55. Approximately what fraction of the data lies between 18 and 40?
questions.explanation: Between Q1 (18) and Q3 (40) lies the middle 50% = 1/2 of the data. This is exactly what the box represents. Each section of a box plot contains approximately 25% of the data.

questions.stem: A box plot for 40 students' marks has Q1 = 32 and Q3 = 56. How many students scored between 32 and 56?
questions.explanation: Between Q1 and Q3 lies the middle 50% of data. 50% of 40 = 20 students. The box in a box plot always represents the interquartile range, containing the middle half of the data.
